name: Proper Equivalence Queries Complexity of Half-intervals
details: More precisely, $\Theta(\log_2 n)$, with endpoint-rounding depending on the threshold convention.
proof: Maintain the interval of feasible right endpoints and query its median initial segment.  A counterexample tells on which side of the queried boundary the target endpoint lies, so the interval is halved at each query.  Conversely, against a query $[k]$, an adversary can answer at $k$ and retain all targets ending before $k$, or answer at $k+1$ and retain all targets ending at or after $k+1$; it chooses the larger side.  Thus logarithmically many proper equivalence queries are both sufficient and necessary.
